correctness.rationale: For any q>=2,m>=1 exactly two deletions are considered. Symmetric embedding of a palindromic receiver in a palindrome parent reduces to one insertion into its half and gives exactly 1+m(q-1) distinct parents. For a nonpalindromic receiver, stripping equal endpoints leaves two unequal outer letters; each of two possible parent outer letters gives an odd residual word with at most one even-palindromic one-insertion parent, proving <=2. Exhibited two-parent witnesses make the bound sharp. Verified independently for all 22 enumerated (q,m) families, 2609 source words. Only the proof yields all-parametric validity.

value.rationale: The exact worst-case list size and all maximizing receiver characterization quantify an intrinsic synchronization decoding ambiguity across all lengths and alphabets.
